figure_alt.Z13-P33: A household of four. Left: the minimum of 1 gallon per person per day for 3 days drawn as a grid of 12 one-gallon jugs, one row per person and one column per day. Centre: the 2-week goal of 56 gallons drawn as eleven 5-gallon containers and one 1-gallon jug. Right: more water for pregnancy, illness, pets or a hot climate, and storage in a cool place (50 to 70 degrees F) out of direct sunlight and away from gasoline and pesticides. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z04-P50: Top: a two-year timeline with self-filled drinking water replaced every 6 months (refill marks at 0, 6, 12, 18 and 24 months, drawn to scale); commercial bottled water follows its printed date. Lower left: containers are replaced when they leak, the cap swells, the plastic turns brittle or the water smells. Lower right: water is stored cool (50 to 70 degrees F), out of direct sunlight and away from fuel and pesticides, with a portable portion ready for evacuation. Conceptual, not to scale apart from the timeline.
figure_alt.Z13-P36: Three advisory tiers. Boil Water: germs; bring tap water to a full rolling boil for 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 feet), even if it was filtered, and use bottled or boiled water for drinking, food and brushing teeth; use ready-made infant formula when available. Do Not Drink: chemicals or toxins; use bottled water for drinking, cooking, brushing teeth, washing produce, formula, ice and pets; boiling does not make the water safe. Do Not Use: any contact may be dangerous; use bottled water for every purpose. During any advisory, no water or ice from refrigerator dispensers. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z13-P43: Left: every year a laboratory certified for drinking-water testing checks the well for total coliform bacteria, nitrate, total dissolved solids and pH. Centre: test again after flooding, well repair or a change in taste, odour or colour, and before bringing a new baby home; test more often where small children, elderly adults, or pregnant or nursing people live. Right: boiling evaporates water but leaves the nitrate, so the same nitrate ends up in less water; above 10 mg/L nitrate use bottled water, especially for formula for babies under six months. Conceptual, not to scale.
figure_alt.Z04-P19: Left: a flooded street carries sewage from an overflowing pipe, a drum of hazardous waste, debris and a downed power line in the water; the person on dry ground stays out of the water and never walks or drives across a flooded road. Right: drinking water comes from stored or sealed supplies and official distribution until local officials say how the water can be used; food or drink touched by floodwater can cause diarrheal disease. Conceptual, not to scale.
